publisher: Vermont Department for Children and Families (DCF), Child Development Division
ownership: Vermont Child Care Provider Data ctdw-tmfz; Child Development Division Data Unit. Licensed Provider rows of CBCCPP or CBCCPP - Non-Recurring only.
allowed_use: internal immutable retention, offline verification and subsequent normalization with provenance and quality gaps
prohibited_use: home-provider and afterschool acquisition under this profile
contact fields, person IDs, explicit mailing-only columns, coordinates or cached catalog samples
inferring exact reporting date from filename or current operation from cohort membership
claiming verified physical premises, exact address geocodes or unique business identity
unrestricted public redistribution or combined database exports
attribution: Vermont DCF Child Development Division; data.vermont.gov; Open Database License 1.0. Preserve source attribution and license notice with retained and derived evidence.
retention: Preserve immutable verified acquisitions for offline reuse and ordinary failure journals for inspection. No automatic deletion or replacement of production pointers.
redistribution: Internal source-separated use only. Public use and combined exports require separate ODbL notice, share-alike and access assessment; individual content and privacy rights remain separate.
personal_data_handling: Center names and reported addresses can incidentally identify people. Exclude family-home categories, contacts, BFIS Person Record IDs and coordinate values; do not enrich people.
authorization_basis: Existing user authorization to collect authorized US business data, verified official ODbL catalog designation and bounded internal source-candidate retention. No account, credential or click-through was used; licensed use remains conditional.
semantic_boundary: file_name plus license_id is a release-scoped source key, not an eternal business identifier. Preserve unknown reporting period, raw license dates, unspecified address role and absent reported state. Omit jittered points; ZIP5 and ZIP4 remain separate in subsequent normalization. Center cohorts may include public programs; they are not all private or verified currently operating businesses.
